questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of four-letter words that can be formed with letters $a, b, c$& such that all three letters occur is
questions.solution:
Out of given three letters $a, b, c$, we will repeat exactly one of the letter and we can do this in $C1 3$ ways.

Now, we have four letters and out of these four letters two are identical, so number of ways to arrange these four letters is $\dfrac{4 !}{2 !}$.

So, the number of four letter words that can be formed with letters $a, b, c$ such that all three letters occur is $C1 3 \times \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} = 36$

$= \left({26}^{2} + {21}^{2}\right)\left({26}^{2} - {21}^{2}\right) - {5}^{4}$

$= \left(676 + 441\right)\left(5\right) \left(47\right) - {5}^{4}$

$= 5\left[\left(1117 \times47\right) - 125\right]$

$= 5 \times \left(52374\right) = 261870
